overview: Angola is a country on the Atlantic coast of southern Africa. Its capital and largest city is Luanda. Angola became independent from Portugal in 1975, and a long civil war followed that ended in 2002. Portuguese is the official language, and Angola is one of Africa's biggest oil producers; Cabinda, a province cut off from the rest of the country by DR Congo, produces much of the oil.

geography.text: Angola has a narrow coastal plain, behind which the land rises sharply to a high central plateau. The north is covered by tropical forest and grassland, while the south-west includes part of the Namib Desert. Many rivers begin in Angola's highlands, including tributaries of the Congo and the Zambezi.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical in the north, dry desert in the south-west along the Namib.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Giant sable antelope, a national symbol, and forest elephants.

history.text: The Kingdom of Kongo and the Ndongo kingdom ruled parts of the region when the Portuguese arrived in the late 1400s. Angola became a centre of the Atlantic slave trade, and Portugal ruled it for centuries. After a long war of independence, Angola became independent in 1975, but a civil war followed that lasted until 2002.

events.title: Portuguese arrive
events.text: Portuguese sailors reach the mouth of the Congo River.

events.title: Queen Nzinga
events.text: Nzinga of Ndongo and Matamba begins decades of resistance to Portugal.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Angola becomes independent and civil war begins.

events.title: Civil war ends
events.text: A ceasefire ends 27 years of war.

government.text: Angola is a presidential republic. The President, who is the leader of the party that wins the parliamentary election, is head of state and government. The MPLA party has governed since independence in 1975. José Eduardo dos Santos ruled for 38 years until 2017.

economy.text: Oil makes up most of Angola's exports, and it is one of Africa's biggest oil producers. It also mines diamonds. Despite this wealth, many people live in poverty. Angola left OPEC in 2024.

culture.text: Portuguese is the official language, and Angolan music and dance, such as semba and kizomba, are popular across the Portuguese-speaking world. Kuduro, an energetic dance music, began in Luanda's streets in the 1990s.

items.title: Kizomba
items.text: A slow, close dance from Angola, now popular worldwide.

items.title: Kuduro
items.text: Fast electronic dance music born in Luanda.

items.title: Kalandula Falls
items.text: One of Africa's largest waterfalls by volume.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Muamba de galinha, chicken stew with palm oil, and funge, a cassava porridge.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Luanda's carnival takes place each February.

sport.text: Basketball is hugely popular, and Angola has won the African championship more than any other country. Its women's handball team is one of Africa's best. Angola played at the 2006 football World Cup.

items.title: AfroBasket
items.text: Angola's men have won the African title 11 times.

didYouKnow: Angola's Kalandula Falls are among the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume.
Kizomba dance, now popular worldwide, began in Angola.

keyPeople.name: Bonga
keyPeople.text: One of Angola's most famous musicians.
